newsitem.title: USA: Former 'Mouseketeer' sues Disney over robbery.
newsitem.headline: Former 'Mouseketeer' sues Disney over robbery.

text.p: Disneyland went on trial on Tuesday, with a former Mouseketeer saying her family was robbed in the attraction's parking lot and her grandchildren traumatized when Disney characters took off their costumes.
After an effort to settle the suit out of court failed, Billie Jean Matay pressed ahead with her claim, charging the Walt Disney Co. for negligence, false imprisonment and emotional distress.

Matay's lawyer told a Superior Court jury that Matay returned in August 1995 to the theme park she helped open 40 years earlier with her daughter and grandchildren, only to be robbed at gunpoint in the parking lot.

Matay claimed in her lawsuit that security in the parking lot was lax, the park's guards were slow to come to her aid, and that she and her family were taken to a backstage area where they were detained by guards and interrogated for several hours against their will.
The suit also claimed that Matay's three grandsons, then aged between 5 and 10, were traumatized by the sight of Disneyland characters they believed were real removing their costumes.
Matay is seeking unspecified damages against her former employer in a civil trial expected to last 10 days.
During opening arguments Tuesday, lawyers for both sides dwelled on the security in the Disneyland parking area, which covers several acres (hectares).

Matay's attorney, Robert O'Connor, evoked the dream of the park's founder, the late Walt Disney, that it should be a safe haven, while Disney's attorney, Stephen Waimey, told the jury about the harsh realities of life in urban America.

"The bottom line is it (the robbery) was an act of urban crime," Waimey told the panel of six men and six women. "Disneyland had no ability to stop it. It was an unfortunate incident but this is a modern world ... an urban world, and crime is a fact of life," he added.

But that, said O'Connor, was not how Walt Disney saw his then-revolutionary park. He quoted the entertainment mogul as saying "the safety and comfort of guests" was Disneyland's highest priority and that visitors to the park "come into a different world that's safe and secure."
Disneyland is located in Anaheim, about 30 miles (50 km) south of Los Angeles.
O'Connor said the robber, who was not caught, stuck a gun to Matay's head and threatened to kill her in front of her daughter and grandchildren before making off with $1,650 in cash and credit cards.
The robber and his accomplice had been allowed to drive into the parking lot by a guard after they said they were there to pick up a relative, O'Connor said.
